altText: Upright photograph of the Toitū Te Whenua Our Whakapapa exhibition panel headed 1980–1989, showing text and historical photographs.
caption: Toitū Te Whenua’s Our Whakapapa panel on DOSLI and digital land-information work during 1980–1989, photographed on 16 October 2026. The GPS date shown in the panel is disputed by an existing chapter source.
dateDisplay: Historical panel period: 1980–1989; photograph taken: 16 October 2026
context: The panel says that district offices began moving from paper to electronic data systems in the 1980s and that teams in all 12 offices digitised cadastral record sheets for the DCDB. LINZ independently places cadastral-map digitisation in the mid-1980s. The panel dates New Zealand’s first GPS survey to Fiordland in March 1989; Te Ara gives 1986, and Chapter 18 treats 1986 as the earliest identified survey while noting that the original survey record remains unrecovered. No 1989 first-survey event is added. The panel photograph was taken on 16 October 2026; that is the capture date, not the date of the historical events described. The original JPEG is preserved unchanged; the full-size display and card variants apply EXIF orientation 6 without cropping.
derivativesNote: The supplied original JPEG bytes are retained unchanged under the source filename. Its EXIF Orientation 6 is applied to the full-resolution WebP and the card WebP; both keep the complete panel in frame without cropping. The original can be downloaded from this page.
